subtype: Hunger and sleep turn into tantrums [Actor]
passage: "No! Blue cup!" Chaitanya flings the red cup and drops flat on the kitchen floor, kicking. "He hardly ate lunch," Amma says from the stove. "Too busy with his blocks." Lalit, his father, crouches beside him. "Nobody is fighting you, little one. Come, roti first." "No roti!" Chaitanya wails, but he opens his mouth when Lalit holds out a warm piece. He chews, hiccups, chews again. Two bites later he points at the red cup. "Water." Lalit laughs softly. "Same cup. Different boy."

qa.q: What did Chaitanya fling before he dropped to the floor?
qa.a: He flung the red cup, shouting that he wanted the blue cup.

qa.q: Why was Chaitanya so upset over which cup he got?
qa.a: He was hungry because he hardly ate lunch, so a small thing like the cup colour felt huge to him.

qa.q: Which choice turned the moment around for Chaitanya?
qa.a: Lalit stopped arguing about the cup and offered warm roti; once Chaitanya had eaten, the fuss faded and he happily asked for water in the red cup.

qa.q: How might Lalit see the cup fight once Chaitanya has eaten?
qa.a: Lalit can see the cup was never the real problem; the same boy is calm now that his tummy is full, which is why Lalit laughs instead of feeling defeated.

grounding: It shows a hungry toddler melting down over a small thing and calming once he eats, with food coming before any reasoning.

subtype: Hunger and sleep turn into tantrums [Actor]
passage:
Note for Shreya's parents, Tuesday
Shreya slept only twenty minutes at nap time today. At snack she cried hard because her banana broke in half, and she pushed the plate away. I didn't ask her to say sorry. I dimmed the lights and patted her back until she slept again, another full hour. When she woke she ate both halves happily and shared her crackers 🙂 We'll keep her nap corner quiet this week.
– Manjula, toddler room

qa.q: How long did Shreya sleep at nap time before the banana upset?
qa.a: Shreya slept only twenty minutes at nap time.

qa.q: What was Shreya likely feeling when the broken banana made her cry so hard?
qa.a: She was very tired after such a short nap, so a small disappointment felt unbearable, which shows in her crying hard and pushing the plate away.

qa.q: What choice did Manjula make at the turning point, and why did it help?
qa.a: Manjula skipped the lesson about manners and helped Shreya sleep again; once rested, Shreya was happy to eat the broken banana and even share.

qa.q: How might Shreya's parents read this note differently from a report that just said she threw her plate?
qa.a: They learn the cause was tiredness, not naughtiness, so they can focus on her rest instead of worrying about her behaviour 😊

grounding: A caregiver's note shows a sleep-short toddler melting down over a broken banana and recovering after more sleep, before any talk of manners.

subtype: Hunger and sleep turn into tantrums [Actor]
passage: The bus home from the weekly haat was late and crowded. Bhupen, not yet two, arched his back and wailed when his sister took the window seat. Alka told him gently to take turns. He screamed louder, rubbing his eyes with both fists. She stopped talking, broke open a boiled sweet potato from her cloth bag and held him on her shoulder. He ate half, slumped, and slept before the river bridge. At home he woke smiling and patted his sister's cheek.

qa.q: What did Alka break open from her cloth bag?
qa.a: She broke open a boiled sweet potato from her cloth bag.

qa.q: What do Bhupen's eye-rubbing and arching suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: They suggest he was tired, hungry and frustrated after the long day at the haat, so losing the window seat felt like too much for him.

qa.q: What was the turning point on the bus, and why did it work?
qa.a: Alka stopped explaining about taking turns and gave him food and her shoulder to sleep on; his body needed that first, and afterwards he was sweet to his sister again.

qa.q: What is the bus ride like for Bhupen's sister?
qa.a: At first she may feel blamed or bothered by his screaming over the seat, but later she gets a friendly pat on the cheek from a rested, happier brother.

grounding: A rural bus ride shows a tired, hungry toddler melting down over a seat and becoming calm after food and a nap.

subtype: Hunger and sleep turn into tantrums [Actor]
passage:
At the supermarket checkout in Vancouver, Ines, two, threw herself on the floor because her sock was twisted. She kicked and screamed, "No sock! No!"
It was long past lunch, and she had skipped her nap. Her dad, Bao, knelt beside her and didn't argue about the sock. He peeled a banana.
Ines grabbed it, still hiccuping, and ate every bite. Ten minutes later she was asleep in the stroller, sock still twisted.

qa.q: What was Ines's complaint at the checkout?
qa.a: Her sock was twisted.

qa.q: What was Ines feeling underneath her screaming over the sock?
qa.a: She felt hungry and worn out, long past lunch and without her nap, so a small thing felt unbearable.

qa.q: Which of Bao's choices worked, and why?
qa.a: He skipped arguing about the sock and gave her a banana, meeting her hunger first, which calmed her enough to fall asleep.

qa.q: How might the other shoppers have seen Ines on the floor?
qa.a: They might have thought she was being naughty, not knowing she was simply hungry and exhausted.

grounding: It shows a toddler melting down over a small thing when hungry and tired, and settling once she eats and sleeps.

subtype: Hunger and sleep turn into tantrums [Actor]
passage:
I'm Leela, Seema's cousin, eleven. At my Mama's engagement party it was nearly ten at night, and Seema, who is two, screamed because I had the pink balloon and she had a yellow one. She lay on the carpet, howling.
Chachi, her mother, just picked her up and fed her a few spoons of dal rice. Seema ate, rubbing her eyes, and fell asleep across two chairs.
Next morning she toddled over and gave me her yellow balloon, smiling.

qa.q: How old is Seema?
qa.a: Seema is two.

qa.q: Why did Seema scream about the balloon, according to what happened after?
qa.a: She was hungry and very tired late at night, so the balloon colour felt huge; once she ate and slept she was happy again.

qa.q: What did Chachi do well, and why did it help?
qa.a: She didn't scold Seema about the balloon; she fed her and let her sleep, which dealt with what Seema really needed.

qa.q: How might Leela feel when Seema gives her the yellow balloon the next morning?
qa.a: Leela might feel surprised and amused, seeing that the screaming girl from the party was just tired and is sweet again after sleep.

grounding: It shows, through a cousin's eyes, a toddler melting down over a small thing when hungry and tired, and the mood changing after food and sleep.
